title: A run's record lives in the plan and in git
description: The gate runner appends every run to an evidence ledger beside the plan, and the readers that grew on it are no longer only a cache of a verdict: the time per task, the repeat of a step whose inputs did not change, the drive's reading of a run it launched in the background, the reading of a red against the base, and the binding of a commit to the run that graded it all read ledger rows. A design that only says the ledger's writes go away would take those with it. So the record moves first, the readers follow through one seam, and the writes stop last, each step with a green gate behind it. The plan and git are the two stores that remain; a row already written stays readable as frozen history and is never migrated. The properties are written before the code: after any number of recorded runs a subject holds exactly one record, the last one printed; a run that exits 0 or 1 has its record in the shard and a record that could not be written is exit 3 naming the log, never exit 0; the pointer is derivable from the record; a decision read from the record equals the run's own output for green and red with no commit made; a recorded run changes no byte inside the content identity; a plan and ledger written by the previous release answer the same after the upgrade, and with the ledger deleted the gate conditions still answer the same. Out of scope here and next in line: the drive's own state, the filed returns, the brief protocol and the subagent writer.
desiredOutcome: A task's verdict is in its commit's Audit-Task, Audit-Gate and Audit-Run trailers, the newest run of every task and phase is one record in its own shard, a phase's CI run is in its shard, every reader of recorded runs goes through one reader over those records and the frozen older rows, the base is measured only when a red could predate the task, and no evidence row, per-call journal row or preimage file is written under the default configuration.

findings.issue: The seven install steps are written out twice, and the only thing holding them together is a comment ('a change to one is owed to the other', ci.yml:~356). Nothing compares them, so a later edit to one job (a package-name tweak, a key change) leaves the other on the old shell with every gate green. The task's own dependants named gate-parity.py's matrix rules; none covers this.
findings.resolution: Move the steps into a composite action (.github/actions/browser-install/action.yml) that both jobs call, or add a gate-parity rule that fails when the two jobs' install step lists differ. Either replaces the prose rule with a mechanism.

findings.issue: The step title 'the archive is asked only for a .deb the restored set lacks' and the log line 'not in the restored set, so fetched from the archive: $fetch' say the archive is asked for the missing .deb. The code passes $MISSING, not $fetch, to apt-get install --download-only, and apt sees only the fresh $dl directory, so on a partial set the archive is asked for the whole set plus its dependency closure and cp overwrites the restored files. The result is correct (that .deb is fetched), but the claim is narrower than the behaviour and only the miss path was exercised on a real runner. Separately, the ls check names only the packages in $MISSING, so a restored set missing a dependency-only .deb (a package apt pulled in that playwright did not name) is not detected and dpkg -i fails with an unmet dependency: a red job, not a green one.
findings.resolution: Either reword the title and log line to say the whole set is refetched when any one is absent, or install $fetch and let the dependency closure follow. Optionally verify the restored set with `dpkg-deb --info` per file, or by `dpkg -i` failing over into one refetch.

findings.issue: A poisoned or truncated cache entry is permanent. Cache keys are immutable and an exact hit is never re-saved, so a bad .deb in a saved entry makes dpkg -i fail (red) on every run of that branch until the key changes or GitHub evicts it, and the step has no path that drops a restored set it cannot install. The same holds for the partial set in finding 2: the repair is not persisted, so each later run repeats the full fetch. The entry can only come to hold a bad file if the job that saved it was green, so this is unlikely, and every outcome seen in the shell is red, not a green job without the packages. The sysdeps key also omits runner.arch, which the browser key carries; a .deb for another architecture would be refused by dpkg (red).
findings.resolution: Add a manual version token to the sysdeps key (chromium-sysdeps-v1-...) so a poisoned entry can be bypassed without a code change, include runner.arch in it, and on a dpkg -i failure fall back once to the fetch path before failing.

findings.issue: The descriptive line says 'The browser jobs' install drops from 3-9 minutes to 12-26 seconds'. The before figures are slow-mirror runs; the after figures come from two fast-mirror runs, and the pre-change install on a fast mirror was 38s (run 41322244766). The change's measured saving is the 21s to 12s (panel) and 26s to 15s (report) between the miss and hit runs, and a miss on a slow mirror costs what it cost before, minus the upgrades. The ci.yml comments say exactly this; the outcome summary does not. Also, main's push runs skip the browser jobs, so main saves no entry and the first run on a new ci/ branch misses both caches, so the hit path may be the rarer one in this repo's own practice; nothing here measures the hit rate.
findings.resolution: State in the outcome that the measured install is 12-26s on a fast mirror on both paths and that the slow-mirror saving is a hit-only saving not measured; decide separately whether a workflow_dispatch on main should seed the caches.

findings.issue: The new behaviour, a verified push to main running the browser jobs with seed true, was executed by no real run. All four logs read 'seed: false' and show seen-browser and seen-sysdeps as outcome=skipped (run2-browserpanel lines 250-253); the plan step took its 'SEED != true' early exit. So actions/cache/restore@v6 with lookup-only, the cache-hit output read by the plan step, the 'entry exists for both keys, nothing installed' branch, the 'one key missing' branch and the workflow's `seed: needs.verified.outputs.run != ''` wiring have been shown only on the uncommitted stub harness. The task's acceptance 1 asked for 'a run on the default-branch path that saves the entries'; the probes were workflow_dispatch runs on a ci/ branch, which exercise the install and the save but not the seed decision. The first real execution of the seed path will be a push to main.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.14-6l3 (2efb8e367eb6): Before landing, push one more probe commit to a ci/ branch with `seed: true` hard-wired and the slice step skipped, and read two runs: the first must print 'seed: no entry exists for the browser key and the system packages' key' then save; the second must print 'seed: an entry exists for every key this image needs, so nothing is installed and nothing is saved' and show every later step skipped. Add a third look at a run with only one of the two keys present if a cheap way exists (a changed BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION on one key is not possible, so state that this half stays stub-only).

findings.issue: Nothing in the repository guards the action's shell besides a real CI run. I searched tracked files: no test, lint or checker names .github/actions or action.yml (git grep for 'action.yml|.github/actions|actionlint|shellcheck' over tools/tests/.claude/plugins finds nothing), gate-parity.py reads only ci.yml, and the 20-case stub harness the proofs rest on (scratchpad stubs/harness.py) is not committed. The first real run found three defects the stubs could not see (Permission denied from cp -a, the image version in the key, jc0). The failure shape is also quiet: any bug that makes the hit path throw lands in `why`, the fallback fetches from the archive, and the job stays GREEN with one ::warning:: and a cache that never helps. No gate reads that warning, so the regression the whole task exists to remove (a first run paying the archive) can return with every check green. A later change (apt flags, BROWSER_CACHE_VERSION, a new package) has only a 13-minute hosted run as feedback and nothing that notices a hit turning into a fallback.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.14-6l3 (2efb8e367eb6): Commit the harness as tests/test_browser_install.py with the `N/M cases passed` contract: extract the `run:` bodies from action.yml by step id, run them under the stub PATH, and keep si1-si10 and the sk/sp cases (full hit asks nothing, miss, partial, dependency missing, unreadable .deb falls back once, fallback failing is red). Add one case that fails when the hit path prints the ::warning:: (the hit must not fall back). If a suite is out of scope for this task, file it as the next task and name it in the outcome; the claim that the install is guarded cannot rest on an uncommitted harness.

findings.issue: An untouched sentence this diff makes false, which the return's claim 3 dismisses as 'pre-existing inexactness about verified unchanged by this task'. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:7699 reads 'a push to main whose commit a run already verified runs only tools/ci-verified.py'. Before this change that was exact (every other job was skipped by `needs.verified.outputs.run == ''`); after it the two browser jobs run their checkout, setup, npm ci, lookups and install on that push. The task named 'the push-to-default-branch path that skips work for a verified commit' as a dependant to answer for by name, and this document is the one that describes that path outside CONTRIBUTING.md.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.14-6l3 (2efb8e367eb6): Change the sentence to say that such a push runs `verified` and, in the two browser jobs, the install only (seeding the caches), and correct claim 3 so it lists this line as made false by the task rather than left. The same pass should re-read tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py:1429, tools/lints/_refs.py:1915 and CLAUDE.md:314 ('every job is setup plus one verify.sh call'), which stay inexact only about `verified` and are unchanged by this diff.

findings.issue: On a push to main whose commit is verified, the browser jobs now do work that can fail: npm ci and `playwright install-deps --dry-run` run before the seed decision even when both entries exist (they are needed only to name the keys), and a miss runs apt and the Chromium download. A transient npm, apt or network failure turns that main run red for a cache it did not need. That is the failure class the `verified` job exists to remove (its own comment: re-running the same bytes 'could only add a ... intermittent the first draw did not have'). It does not skip any slice, and no gate reads main's run, so the cost is a red check on an already-verified commit, not a lost verdict.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.14-6l3 (2efb8e367eb6): Give the two jobs `continue-on-error: ${{ needs.verified.outputs.run != '' }}` so a failed seed is visible but not red, or compute the playwright pin and image name without npm ci on the seed path. Say in ci.yml which is chosen.

findings.issue: On main a running run is never cancelled and one pending run is held; a third push replaces the pending one, which then never runs. A verified push used to finish in about half a minute; it now holds the group for the seed's duration (a hit: checkout, node, npm ci, two lookups; a miss: the full install, 2m20s on the measured fast-mirror miss and up to the install's 9m22s fetch on a slow day). A commit queued behind a seeding miss is more likely to be replaced and get no run on main.
findings.resolution: State it in the comment above browser-panel as a cost of seeding, or have the seed job take its own concurrency group (`concurrency: browser-seed`) so it does not hold ci-refs/heads/main.

findings.issue: Two statements go past what the logs show. (a) outcome.descriptive says 'a hit asks the archive for nothing on any image version of the distribution'; one cross-image restore was measured (set saved on 20261111.127.1, restored on 20261111.370.1) and the action's own header (action.yml:27-44) says an image whose installed versions the set's index cannot satisfy falls back to a fresh fetch and keeps doing so on every run. (b) outcome.technical attributes the report job's 35s after the restore to 'apt Reading package lists 18s plus dpkg Reading database about 10s'. In run2-browserreport the 'Reading package lists...' line is 20:12:41.008 and the dependency listing follows at 20:12:41.34; the 18.5s gap is between 'The following NEW packages will be installed' (20:12:41.348) and '0 upgraded, 9 newly installed' (20:12:59.923), which is not apt's index read. The panel job's same stretch took 2.6s (20:12:30.0 to 20:12:32.6), so the gap is variable and unexplained, not shown to be local.
findings.resolution: Write (a) as 'on the image versions measured' and (b) as 'an unexplained 18s between the dependency listing and the summary line, not seen in the panel job'. The committed comments already avoid both claims; only the return's wording needs the change.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "the recorder takes the phase lock with a bounded wait behind any verb's write" and acceptance 4 ("a verb's write and a background record write, interleaved in both orders, both land"). write_record takes `phase-<id>`, but every audit-task.py verb reads and writes the shard under the INDEX lock (`_under_lock` -> `_panel_write.acquire_index_lock`, LOCK_NAME "index" at _panel_write.py:392); the only `phase-<id>` holders are `start`'s claim and the drive's phase run. So a verb's read-modify-write and the recorder's are not mutually exclusive. Probe in a scratch copy: index lock held by a stand-in verb, write_record returned written=True after 0.02s without waiting, then the verb's write from its earlier read left the shard with neither lastRun nor testEvidence (and the reverse order loses the verb's write, e.g. a `done`). lr4 passes only because its stand-in verb takes `phase-P1`, which no real verb does; lr5 ("the other order") asserts only what the test's own read-modify-write does and goes red only when lr4's landing is missing (M1 and M2 each reddened it as a knock-on). CHANGELOG, manifest-conventions.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md repeat the claim ("so neither write loses the other's key"). The old pointer write had the same exposure; what is new is the claim, and that the shard now holds the only copy of the record and of the stages.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.15-6l3 (9de731d5adb6): Make the recorder's write exclude the verbs: take the index lock as well as the phase lock (one fixed order, checked against `start`, which takes `phase-<id>` while a verb holds the index lock), or have the verbs' shard writes take the phase lock. Re-aim lr4 so the stand-in verb takes the lock real verbs take (drive a real `audit-task.py note` against the same project), and either give lr5 a product assertion or drop it. Until then, correct the three documents so they promise what is true: a wait behind `phase-<id>` holders only.

findings.issue: The repeated-verdict arm has no case, and it fails silent. Deleting the copy (`steps = []` for the `source` branch) left test__evidence_io 361/361 and test_run_test_gate 699/699 green (M6, both suites run in a scratch copy): every lr case runs with `--no-reuse`, and no case passes `source=` to run_record. The clause "a copied step carries its source's verdict fields forward, so ... no older record is needed to read it" is therefore shown by nothing. The source is read only from the ledger row (`row_by_run`); when that row is not there - the day the later task stops writing rows, or a rotated ledger - the record is `steps: []` with `verdictSource: reused` and no marker that its steps are unavailable (probe: run_record(reused_row, source=None) -> steps []). Separately, the record keeps the read-back's own startedAt and durationMs (probe: durationMs 120, startedAt of the repeat) while the schema says startedAt is "absent on a run that repeated another's verdict, which measured nothing", and nothing on the record separates those figures from a measurement except `verdictSource`.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.15-6l3 (9de731d5adb6): Add a gate-level case (reuse on, second run) and a run_record(source=...) case asserting the copied steps, their per-step reusedFrom and the absence of per-step durationMs; take the source from the subject's previous `lastRun` when the ledger row is gone, and say `stepsUnavailable` (or equivalent) when neither is there rather than writing an empty list. For a repeated run either omit startedAt/durationMs/selectionMs from the record or state in the schema that they are the read-back's own.

findings.issue: Two writers of one key can leave `testEvidence` naming a run other than `lastRun`, against the doc's "the two always name one run" and COMPATIBILITY's "runId, status and at in it are the values testEvidence caches". reconcile takes the ledger row when it is stamped after the record (the run whose record write was refused, exit 3) and calls write_pointer, which moves only the pointer; lastRun keeps the older run. Also write_pointer still reads the shard BEFORE it takes the lock (read_json at 2542, acquire at 2553, save at 2567), so a reconcile racing a recorder saves its stale body over the recorder's lastRun and timing stages. The task's clause says reconcile does to lastRun what it does to testEvidence.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.15-6l3 (9de731d5adb6): In reconcile, when the ledger row wins, also write `run_record(row)` so the pair stays one run, or soften the two sentences to "names one run except after a refused record write, until the next recorded run". Read the shard under the lock in write_pointer, as write_record now does (share `_holders`).

findings.issue: Stale text contradicts the new behaviour: the `--record` help reads "a green run whose row could not be stored exits 3 (0 passed, 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 passed but unrecorded)" and the E_UNRECORDED comment says "the gate is green and the record the caller asked for does not exist"; a red run now exits 3 as well (lr6), and `unrecorded_line` says so. A pre-push or CI step reading `--help` is told that 1 is always the work's failure.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.15-6l3 (9de731d5adb6): Reword both to "a run (green or red) whose row or whose record in the plan could not be stored exits 3".

findings.issue: A stale phase lock is refused at once, with no wait (probe: dead holder, wait=5, returned in 0.00s), so every recorded gate of that phase exits 3 until a human runs `audit-lock --takeover`; that is the designed rule, but the sentence it prints is garbled by the hint: "...use audit-lock --takeover, then nothing was written to the plan". It names no repair, and the gate's own closing line says "re-run once the phase lock is free" for a run that may have taken minutes.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.15-6l3 (9de731d5adb6): Pass a hint that names the repair ("then re-run this gate; nothing was written to the plan") so both the stale and the held sentences read, and say in `unrecorded_line` that the ledger row stands, so `--reconcile` is not mistaken for the repair of a missing record.

findings.issue: The drive finds the run it launched by a launch token that exists only on the plan's record; the ledger row never carries it, and the union adds it to a row only while the record still holds that same run. When another run of the same subject is recorded after the launched one (a hand-run /audit:run, a sibling session, /audit:review during a background phase gate), or the launched run's record write was refused on the lock, run_by_launch returns None for good and the drive keeps answering wait-gate with 'no gate row ... since', which is false: the ledger holds the row. The code this replaced found it. Established by reading and a function-level probe (a ledger row without a token plus a newer record carrying another token gives None); case lt2 covers only the other order.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.16-6l3 (eb1cee095ad1): Put the launch token on the ledger row as well (an identity key of the row), and when the subject's newest run is later than the launch and carries another token, say the launched run was replaced and by which run instead of waiting.

findings.issue: A record still lacks fields readers of the one seam take from a row, so a run held only as a record gives them None or an empty list with nothing saying so: followersOwed (the drive's run_followers returns [], and a red that owes regenerated followers is decided as a plain red), gateReach and its not-asked twin (a repeated verdict prints that the source run recorded no reach reading, which is false), observations, treeMutated and coverage (the panel and the report would say no comparison was made). Masked today because ledger rows are still written. Established by a probe: run_record of a row carrying these kept only at, runId and steps.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.16-6l3 (eb1cee095ad1): Derive the record's keys from what the readers of the seam read rather than from a hand list: carry these fields, and hold the list to the readers with a case that fails when a reader takes a row key the record does not carry.

findings.issue: Several callers of read_rows pass no manifest path, so the records they read are those of the plan the project's config names, while write_record writes to the plan the command was handed. For a command run against another plan in the same project (the examples' plans; task ids such as P1.1 collide), reuse and the lookup of a repeat's source read a foreign plan's records: the repeat's source is not found, or another plan's record is read as this plan's subject. Established by reading; the drive is not affected (its config comes from project_config_for).
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.16-6l3 (eb1cee095ad1): Every caller hands the seam the plan it was handed; make the plan a required argument of the seam so a caller that forgets it is an error rather than a silent default.

findings.issue: The importer refuses a whole ledger file when any of its runs is held as a record in the plan. For a project whose plan travels with git and whose evidence files do not, a run recorded on another machine arrives in the committed shard first, and importing that machine's ledger file is then refused with 'already in <plan file>', losing every other row of the file and the fuller row of that run. The stated reason (a run counted twice) does not apply: the union keeps one entry per run id and the ledger row wins.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.16-6l3 (eb1cee095ad1): Only a run held as a ledger row is a duplicate; a run held only as a record is imported, and the union's own rule decides which copy a reader sees. Cases for both.

findings.issue: Messages still name the ledger alone or print a figure nobody counted: '--base-of' says no run is recorded in the ledger, the drive says the evidence ledger holds no row, the panel's dangling sentence prints '0 files read' and never reads ledgerAbsent (the task's fifth acceptance point), and the binding says no gate verdict is recorded when the subject's shard could not be read.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.16-6l3 (eb1cee095ad1): Each message names both places it looked, and an unreadable shard is said as unreadable with the file.

findings.issue: Plan files that will not read go unreported in three places (close-phase skips an unreadable shard at the tip silently and gives no note when the tip is unreadable but a worktree exists; the importer ignores unreadablePlanFiles), and there are three walkers of a plan's shards with three error rules (plan_bodies, subject_records, close-phase's tip_bodies).
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.16-6l3 (eb1cee095ad1): One walker with one rule for a shard that will not read, used by all three, which reports the file.

findings.issue: Two sentences of the Tests section are no longer exact once the browser jobs carry an install step that a seed run may fail and a warning step: 'every CI job is setup plus one tools/verify.sh --only <slices> call' (already inexact for the verified job), and the enumeration of what gate-parity.py checks lacks the rule that a step or job running a slice is never allowed to fail. Reported by the executor of the cache task; CLAUDE.md is the project's instruction file and is not edited on an agent's report.
findings.resolution: The owner decides the wording; the paragraph already points at gate-parity's docstring as the current statement, so the repair may be to delete the enumeration and keep the pointer.

findings.issue: The new mask replaces ` *\b<duration>` with a fixed ` <duration>`, so it swallows the whole run of spaces between the exit code and the duration as well as the digit-dependent padding. A change to the step line's column layout that only a present-but-empty executor.phaseGateOnly caused (the gap between `exit N` and the duration) is no longer visible to pgo7. Measured in a scratch copy: a runner that, only when the key is present, widens that gap (`exit 0  ` -> `exit 0     `) is FAIL under the old mask and PASS under the new one. The class pgo7 exists for (the setting changing what the runner prints) is still caught for an extra line, a reworded banner, a renamed step, a changed check-count text and a changed duration unit; only pure whitespace layout inside the swallowed gap is lost.
findings.resolution: Keep the layout invariant instead of dropping it: the width of (padding + duration text) is constant for one exit-code width, so substitute with a function that returns `"<duration>".rjust(len(match.group(0)))` (or equivalent) rather than a fixed ' <duration>'. The digit-count-dependent padding then still collapses to one spelling while a real column-width change still reddens the case.

findings.issue: A command the action calls that has no stub runs for REAL. The `sudo` stub is `STUB_USER=root exec "$@"`, so `sudo <anything not stubbed>` executes the host's own tool, as the invoking user, on any path; PATH is the fixture bin plus /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin, and only apt-get, apt-config, mkdir, cp, chown and sudo are stubbed (rm is not). Measured in a scratch copy: appending `sudo rm -rf <scratch>/outside/victim` and `sudo touch <scratch>/outside/made` to the `sysdeps-install` script left the check at '22 of 22 cases held', the victim deleted and `made` created outside the fixture. Today the real `sudo rm -rf "$d"` is HOME-bound only because `d` is spelled from the fixture HOME; an edit to the action that names an absolute path (`sudo rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*`, `sudo tee`, `sudo sh -c`) would run on a developer's machine in the lint slice and under the sweep, and the docstring says only that real sudo, apt and dpkg are never reached. Also `/usr/bin/sudo` by absolute path reaches the real sudo (stdin is inherited, so it can prompt).
findings.resolution: Make the fixture bin the whole of PATH: symlink only the real tools the steps need (sed, ls, printf, tr, cut, sha256sum, id, wc, dirname, bash utilities) next to the stubs, give `rm` a stub that refuses a path outside the fixture root, and make the `sudo` stub exec only a name found in the fixture bin, otherwise print 'unstubbed command under sudo: NAME' and exit 99. Add a selftest row that appends `sudo touch <outside>` to a copy of the action and requires the check red with the file absent. Pass stdin=DEVNULL in run_script.

findings.issue: `longest browser-panel: 7m46s (run 44385960921)` is not the longest recorded run: run 44424245100 (a dispatch, in the diff's own evidence for the report line) has browser (panel) 2026-11-18T23:51:27Z to 2026-11-19T00:02:56Z, 11m29s, success (install 5m59s on a miss, slice 5m00s), per `gh run view 44424245100 --json jobs`. The panel bound stays 18, which is 1.57 times that run, under the two-times rule `job_bound_evidence` states (it passes only because the stale line is still the one it reads). The diff rewrote the report's line from the same family of runs and left the panel's.
findings.resolution: Set `longest browser-panel` to 11m29s (run 44424245100, 23:51:27 to 00:02:56), raise the panel's timeout-minutes to at least 23, and say so in the comment above browser-panel; or state in the comment why that run is not a measurement of this job.

findings.issue: Several plainly broken actions are green. Measured in a scratch copy, each gives '22 of 22 cases held': the `npx playwright install chromium` step deleted; the `npm ci` step deleted; the `sysdeps` step's `key=` line replaced by `key=constant` (the hash and the version gone from the cache key); the `sysdeps-install` step's `missing != ''` guard dropped; `seed` defaulting to "true"; and the system packages' key expression changed to the same other value in both the lookup and its restore (sd1 only compares them with each other). The docstring discloses that npm ci, Chromium and the dry run are not run, but not that the sysdeps step's key output and the restore steps' key expressions are unread, nor that deleting a step passes (sd3 judges only the steps that exist).
findings.resolution: Add to sd: the restore steps' `key:` must equal `${{ steps.pins.outputs.browser-key }}` and `${{ steps.sysdeps.outputs.key }}`; the Chromium install step and the npm ci step must exist and the Chromium one be guarded by the plan; the `seed` input's default must be "false"; run the sysdeps step's key lines against a stub dpkg-query/npx so the key's parts are read. Add a bm row per property, or state each as unread in the docstring.

findings.issue: The new rule never sees a flow-style step. `- { name: a, continue-on-error: true, run: sh tools/verify.sh --only lint }` gives job_slices zero runs and no problem (measured: problems [] and runs [0]), so a slice allowed to fail by that spelling is neither a finding nor counted as run. The other shapes I tried read correctly: `- continue-on-error:` on the opening line, quoted "true", True, a trailing comment, the key after a `run: |` block, an expression, a job-level key, and `continue-on-error: true` text inside a run block (not read, correctly); the seed's install step beside a guarded verify step is allowed. The step-keys reader does not own this blindness (`_key_line` and `_job_runs` already ignore `- {`) but the new rule's claim is that a slice can never be the thing allowed to fail.
findings.resolution: In `_step_runs`/job_slices, report a `problems` row for any `steps:` item that opens with `{` (or `[`), 'a flow-style step this reader cannot read', and add a case beside sv25.

findings.issue: The documents state the failed-seed behaviour as fact ('A seed never reddens the verified push', 'A failed seed is a warning on the run, not a red job', 'the next step writes a warning annotation'), but no run exercised it. In the runs they cite the seed-true install step succeeded and the warning step was skipped (run 44426388905: `seed: say that the install failed` skipped in both browser jobs; run 44428930205 likewise). The return's unobserved list names only a seed on main and the cross-branch restore, and every place that says 'Not yet seen in a run' omits this path.
findings.resolution: Add 'a seed whose install fails: the conclusion staying green and the warning being written' to the not-yet-seen sentences in ci.yml, CONTRIBUTING.md and the guide, or observe it once on the probe branch with a forced install failure and cite that run.

findings.issue: A failure path leaves a directory behind: `build_fixture` makes `tempfile.mkdtemp` and then does the makedirs and writes, and `_install_case` calls it BEFORE its `try/finally`, so an exception inside build_fixture (full disk, a write refused) leaks the scratch directory into the sweep's watched TMPDIR. All other cases (run_pins, _plan_case, a stub timeout) are cleaned in finally. Separately, on a non-POSIX host the gate is red 'could not run here' for 17 cases, so a local `sh tools/verify.sh` lint slice on Windows fails on a check the CI lint job (ubuntu) never runs there; the verify.sh comment says only that it 'says it could not run'.
findings.resolution: Wrap the body of build_fixture in try/except that rmtree()s root and re-raises, or create root in the caller and rmtree it in the same finally. For the host case either exit 0 with a printed 'skipped: <reason>' from the gate (the selftest already records a skip) or say in verify.sh that the slice is red on a host without POSIX.

findings.issue: A gate the drive launched and that ends cancelled is launched again with nothing bounding it: background_gate reads a cancelled run back and calls launch_gate, which mints a new token, replaces the launch mark and spends nothing; the phase gate path does the same through launch_phase_gate. No attempt is spent, no count is kept and nobody is asked, so a gate that is killed every time (by the shell's own time bound, for one) is dispatched for ever, each round a main-loop turn and a gate run. Not introduced by the lock change: with the drive's own session the cancelled record already landed and this branch already ran; the suite's fixture only read 'wait' because its child had no session and waited out the phase lock. Found by the executor of the lock task when the record began to land in that fixture (case bg4).
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.15-6l3 (9de731d5adb6): Count cancelled relaunches on the launch mark, carried when the mark is replaced, for the task gate and the phase gate through one function; past a bound the drive stops with an ask instead of dispatching. A case that kills the gate past the bound and expects the ask, and bg4 pins the relaunch under a new token below it.

findings.issue: Reconcile can delete the only copy of the run a repeat copied. When run A exists only as the subject's record (a clone or worktree whose ledger never held it: the record travels with the plan), run B repeats A, B's row reaches the ledger and its record write is refused, the documented repair --reconcile looks for B's source among the ledger rows only and has no fallback to the record it is about to replace, so A's record is overwritten by B's carrying the unread marker, A is readable nowhere, and the commit binding then refuses B's verdict as a repeat whose source is gone. The record writer keeps A on the same inputs. Established by a probe (write path: carried RA; reconcile path: carried None, unread True, A no longer readable).
findings.resolution: One helper finds a repeat's source for every writer of a record (the union of ledger rows and records, then the record being replaced), used by the record writer and by reconcile; a case that reconciles a repeat whose source is held only as the record.

findings.issue: Both repair commands read the whole plan before taking the index lock (git lookups run between the read and the acquire) and then save every shard and the index from that earlier read under the lock, so a gate's record or pointer, or any verb's write, made in that window is written back out of existence. Established by a probe for repair-commits (a record R9 present before the repair is None after it) and by reading for repair-tests-add. It predates the lock change, but the change's module comment says the repair commands read-modify-write under the lock, and the cases that hold the one-writer rule read one module's syntax tree only, so a writer outside that module bypasses the rule unseen.
findings.resolution: Both repairs re-read the plan inside the locked section and recompute what they write from that read. The rule is held over every module under scripts/ and hooks/: every caller of a plan save is found by reading the tree, and one that is not in a table of writers shown to read behind the lock (each row with its reason) is red by name.

findings.issue: When the gate runner exits 3 because the index lock was busy past the record's wait, the drive stops with the generic stop instead of the wait-and-run-next-again rule it already has for a verb's exit 3. A background gate mostly recovers (the ledger row is written first and the read-back asks again in the foreground); only if that ask also meets a busy lock does the drive stop on the wrong rule. The one long holder in normal use is the commit verb, which holds the lock across git commit, so a project's pre-commit hook longer than the record's wait refuses the records of wave siblings finishing meanwhile.
findings.resolution: The runner's exit 3 on a busy index lock is read as the same wait rule as a verb's; a case. Say in the guide that the commit verb holds the lock across the commit and what a slow pre-commit hook costs.

findings.issue: When the lock claim cannot be written at all (the lock directory is not writable), the refusal says the index lock was not free within the wait, while the lock module's own line says this is not a report that the lock is held; and the work is refused, where the lock module documents an unwritable claim as refusing the lock and not the work, as the panel's writer and the repairs treat it.
findings.resolution: An unwritable claim has its own sentence, and whether a record is written without the lock in that state is decided explicitly, the same way for every writer through the helper.

findings.issue: Two questions the review could not establish. A converter run under a hand-taken index lock takes no lock itself: is a gate of the same session answered as the holder by session match, so that it writes a shard in the middle of the conversion and the converter's earlier read drops it? And git itself writes plan files with no plugin lock (the merge into the parent checkout, a member tree's records refresh, the merge driver's result): these sit outside the every-writer-takes-the-lock claim, and the documents should say so or the paths should take it.
findings.resolution: Establish each by a probe; fix or state it.

findings.issue: The release guard lets a release through when the run reader raises. A plan that parses but carries a malformed lastRun makes read_rows raise; nothing between read_held_phases, tree_verdict, decide and main catches it, the hook exits 1 with no deny, and an exit 1 from a pre-tool hook does not block, so `git tag` goes ahead. Established by a probe that runs the hook on a tag command: with no record the release is denied; with `lastRun.steps: 5` it is not denied (already so before this change); with `lastRun.recordCut: 5` and with a shared path over a list-valued field it is not denied, and both of those were denied before this change, which added the two functions that raise. The same malformed field raises for every other reader of the seam as well.
findings.resolution: The guard refuses when the recorded runs cannot be read, saying so with the error; and a mistyped field in a record cannot raise for any reader: the record's readers check the shapes they walk and report the record as unreadable with its file and field. Cases for the guard (each malformed shape is a deny) and for the reader.

findings.issue: A record's keys now pass through into the row except a small set, where before only an allow-list did, and the subject id is set from placement only for a task record: a phase record carrying `taskId` reads as a run of that task, and a probe with the ledger absent got a task with no record of its own bound to the phase record's run. Only a hand edit produces it, and editing the task's own record already gives the same power, so nothing new is forgeable, but the protection the allow-list gave is gone.
findings.resolution: record_row drops every key the record is defined not to carry before it applies placement, so identity always comes from where the record sits; a case.

findings.issue: Keys only a record should hold leak into the run a repeat carries when its source was read back from a record: the carried run came back holding launch, replacedLaunches and sharedUnresolved, so a stale marker says something about a run that shares nothing. The sufficiency cases only cover keys a ledger row can hold, which is why they do not see it.
findings.resolution: The record-shaped keys are one table that both directions exclude; a case that carries a source read back from a record.

findings.issue: A relaunch after a replacement starts the cancelled count again at nought, so a launched run that came back cancelled and was replaced before the drive read it puts the bound's ask off; no attempt is spent on such a relaunch and nothing bounds how many there are, and once a launched run's entry is cut from the bounded list of replaced launches the drive waits for ever again, which is what the list exists to prevent. Each step needs another actor recording a run of the same subject in between; two drives on one subject were not reproduced.
findings.resolution: The count is carried across a replacement relaunch (and raised when the replaced run was cancelled), replacement relaunches are counted on the mark and bounded by the same ask, and a launch cut from the list is said as that rather than waited on.

findings.issue: The binding never reads the unresolved-share marker: it still refuses, because the field it reads is then absent, but the sentence names the wrong cause (a missing scope digest, or a gate measured under no steps). No other surface reads the marker either. And the lookup's banner reads a tree-changed observation as an empty list when it was cut from the record, so the banner is silently absent.
findings.resolution: The binding refuses naming the unresolved paths; the lookup says the observation was cut, with the record's own basis.

findings.issue: A red decided beside a running base is not limited to the free resume. The beside branch fires whenever a background base is running for the red, without asking which decision it leads to. With no recorded writer session (a task written by an agent) or with the start's resume rounds spent, the decision is plain gate-red: the orchestrator answers it itself, and `retry` spends an attempt while the base is still unmeasured. Before this change the drive held until the base ended and asked the base decision instead. A red that predates the task now costs the task an attempt, and can block it: each retry is a new start, the old base has recorded nothing yet, so the new start launches a second base on the same commit and is asked plain gate-red again, until the attempts are gone. Established by a probe on the suite's own fixture: with the rounds spent, `--answer retry` took attempts from 1 to 2 with no base row recorded; with no session the decision was plain gate-red beside the base as well. No case pins the shape. The changelog and the executor reference describe the beside decision only as the resume path.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): The red is decided beside a running base only when the decision is the resume that spends nothing; in every other case the drive holds for the base as it did. A second start never launches a second base run of a commit one is already running for. Cases for both shapes, and the documents say which decision may be taken beside.

findings.issue: The skip for a red in the task's own new files tests the spelling in tests.add at the base commit rather than the path the runner named. A name is matched by suffix in either direction, so when tests.add spells a file shorter than the runner does, the shorter path is absent at the root and a file that EXISTS at base is called created by the task: the base run is skipped and a red that may be the base's is charged to the task (probe: a committed tests/unit/test_old.py against the spellings test_old.py and unit/test_old.py). Two related holes: a git failure on the per-path question reads as absent (a suite outside the repository returned the skip sentence), and the skip ignores that the row's suite list was cut, so a step whose carried suites are all the task's own is skipped though a suite past the cut may be an old one.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): The question is asked of the runner's own path, made repository-relative, against the base commit's tree; any answer from git other than a clean not-found means measure; a cut suite list means measure. Cases for each, both directions.

findings.issue: When a red's steps count as measured but the stored reading is stale, the kept base is asked again; if that ask fails (any refusal, unparsable output, or the gate runner's own count disagreeing), the reading stays the row's no-base reading and the red still goes to the writer under the sentence that every red step was measured at base already. The basis is missing and the sentence does not say so; the kept base, unread, may say the red was already there. Established by reading.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): A kept base that cannot be read back falls to measuring, or to the decision that says the base is unknown with the refusal's own words; never to the writer under a sentence about a measurement nobody read. A case with a kept-only ask that refuses.

findings.issue: Only an UNANSWERED beside decision is dropped when the base ends. An answer given after the base ended and before any call re-read it is applied even when the base proved the red was already there: the resume is sent over a red the drive already knows is the base's. Since the decision is the orchestrator's own to answer within seconds, this is the usual timing when the base finishes during its turn. Probe: beside decision, base played to the end as base-only, then `--answer resume` dispatched the writer.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): An answer to a beside decision whose base has ended is refused with a sentence saying the base ended and the decision is taken again; a case.

findings.issue: When a writer resumed beside the base turns the gate green, the base's own red is lost. The base cannot be kept (the subject's newest run reads no red), the base mark is never decided because that happens only on a red path, its stage is never queued to the time record, and nothing tells the reviewer or sign-off that the writer made green a red the base commit already had, possibly by changing a test. The only trace is the ledger's base row, which stops existing when ledger writes go off. Established by reading.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): A green gate whose start holds an ended base mark settles it: the base's verdict is kept where the plan holds it, the time record gets its stage, and when the base had the red the task carries a note the reviewer's brief and the sign-off read. A case.

findings.issue: A base step that reached no verdict (no exit, timed out) counts as measured, so no base is measured again at that commit for that step set, and such a step already reads as green at base, which charges the red to the task. The reading predates this change; keeping runs makes it permanent for the commit.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): A base step counts as measured only when it answered; a case.

findings.issue: The sentence about rounds resumed beside a base counts every resume since the mark went beside for as long as it is done, including rounds resumed after the base had its verdict, and says of all of them that they worked on a red the base already had.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): The count stops at the resume count recorded when the base's end was first read; a case with a round on each side.

findings.issue: The description says kept base runs are the first key a record over its bound loses; the code cuts them last, and the build guide and the module's comment say last.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): The description says what the cut order does, by naming the table rather than a position.

findings.issue: A mutation making keep_base accept a base of another commit survived every block run against it: a second filter hides it, and the visible effect is an answer saying written with nothing kept. No case writes a base of another head.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): A case that hands keep_base a base of another commit and asserts the refusal's sentence and that nothing is written.

findings.issue: The recorder writes a run record the published schema refuses. A record for a reused verdict stores no `steps` (they are shared with the run it repeats and named under sharedWithRepeated) while the schema's lastRun requires `steps`. The first such record was written into this repository's own plan by the committed code, and tests/test_validate_manifest.py sp1 is red on it with the validator's own words: the published schema refuses this value, and validate-manifest will refuse it from 4.0.0 (a warning in 3.x). So from the next major release every plan in which a gate verdict was reused is INVALID by the plugin's own validator, which is in the default set of the status gate. The task that introduced the sharing proved its records against readers and never against the schema; its sweep was green only because no shared record existed in the live plan yet.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.21-6l3 (8b0cfc237783): Every record the recorder can compose (measured, part repeat, whole repeat, shared, cut by the bound, carrying kept or settled base runs, with replaced launches) is one the published schema accepts, held by a case that composes each shape through the writer and validates it with the same reader validate-manifest uses; the schema describes the stored form, including when steps may be absent; this repository's own plan validates with no schema line.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py (the decision taken beside a running base; where an answer is applied)
findings.issue: Second sighting of one class, found reviewing the uncommitted repair of P169-R41: the repair limits the beside decision to the writer decision because its resume spends nothing, but that decision also offers `retry`, which is applied while the base still runs, spends an attempt and sends a fresh writer for a red the base may show it already had (probe on the suite's own fixture: attempts 1 to 2 with the base not done). The repair's own case answers `retry` beside the running base and never reads the attempt count. The rule was placed on the NAME of the decision; what it must bind is the ANSWER.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): While the base of a start's red is unmeasured, no answer that spends is accepted, whatever decision offered it: enforced at the one place answers are applied, from the same table that says which answers spend, with a refusal that spends nothing and says to wait for the base or give an answer that spends nothing. A case walks every decision the drive can print for a red against every answer it offers, derived from the tables, and asserts the attempt count.

findings.issue: The own-files skip still charges the task for a red in a file whose cases predate it, in two shapes probed on a real repository: a file under a directory the task renamed (same file and cases at base under the old path) and, on a case-insensitive filesystem, a path spelled in another letter case than the base's tree holds. A symlink the task created to a base file skips as well.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): The skip holds only for a path the base commit's tree lacks AND that the task's change did not arrive at by a rename or copy of a base file (asked of git with rename detection), compared the way the filesystem compares; a symlink measures. Cases for each, with the twin that still skips.

findings.issue: On a green gate, a mark that joined an earlier start's base run keeps that run's reading under the joined red's name, and when the reading had the red writes a note naming a verdict nobody measured for that run; on the red path the same reading is deliberately refused for the joined red. The two paths contradict each other. Established by reading; reachable through a writer decision beside the base, a resume, then green.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): A settled reading is kept and noted only against the red it was measured for; a joined mark is decided and keeps nothing it did not measure. A case.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py (the green-over-base-red note; beside_ended; JOINED_UNREAD; join_base); CHANGELOG.md; plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md
findings.issue: Sentences that say more than the code does: the note says the writer round resumed beside the base turned the gate green whatever turned it green (a rerun of an unstable case included); an answer after a REPLACED launch is refused as if the base had ended; the joined-unread sentence says no run of the commit was found when one was found that did not measure every step; the join's line says the joined run is still measuring when it never started; the documents say a new start at a commit whose base is running joins it, while only the same task's run is joined.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): Each sentence says what the code knows and names its basis; the documents say which starts join.

findings.issue: Three holes in the cases: no case covers a green gate whose base mark is already decided or still running (a mutation dropping those checks survived every block); the table's default for an unnamed pair is dead code no case reaches (a mutation of it survived); the gate runner's new wording and filter for a base step that reached no verdict have no case in its own suite.
findings.resolution: fixed in P169.22-6l3 (5fb16b90123c): A case for each, or the dead default removed with the table made total by construction.

findings.issue: The arm that admits a record sharing its steps is looser than what the recorder writes, in three ways a standard validator and the repository's reader both show: a record holding BOTH `steps` and a sharing entry naming them is accepted, and on read its own steps are silently replaced by the derived ones; a record naming `steps` as shared with no `repeatedRun` to share with is accepted and reads back as unresolved; and the `contains` in that arm carries no `type`, which adds one strict-mode warning line to the standard validator's run in CI.
findings.resolution: Exactly one of the two arms holds (`oneOf`), the sharing arm requires `repeatedRun`, and `contains` sits beside `type: array`; the twin cases refuse both hand-made records.

findings.issue: The case that holds every composed record shape to the schema is weaker than it reads in two places: four mutations of its own derivation left it green (a table's walk replaced by an empty list passes, because the guards check that the tables are non-empty and not that the comparison walked them), and it composes only passed and failed runs, so the other statuses the runner records (timed out, cancelled, could not run, no checks, empty gate, gate mutated) are never held to the schema. The group copy the task verbs write with `gradedBy` is not composed either.
findings.resolution: Each table's walk is its own conjunct that an empty walk fails; one composed record per status the runner can record, derived from the status table; the group copy composed through its writer.

findings.issue: One clause describes a repair to behaviour no release ever had (that the validator used to warn every such record broke the schema): the record itself is new in this unreleased section, so a reader of the release notes meets a fix for something they never saw.
findings.resolution: The clause goes; the sentence says what the schema accepts.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py (apply_answer, base_refusal, the key recorded only by gate_red_decision)
findings.issue: Third sighting of one class, found reviewing the uncommitted invariant: the refusal of a spending answer over an unmeasured base fires only for a decision that carries a key, and only the red-gate decision writes that key, so a spending decision produced anywhere else goes past it. Reached through the recommended path (probe on the suite's own fixtures): a writer decision is taken beside a base handed out but not started; the person answers the recommended resume; the resumed round produces no result (a crash, the budget running out); the next call asks the no-return decision, which carries no key; `retry` is applied, attempts go 1 to 2, the base is never measured and its launch is orphaned. The derived case proves the refusal given the key, never that every producer records it.
findings.resolution: The state that makes the class possible is removed rather than guarded a fourth time: no decision about a red exists while its base is unmeasured, because the drive holds for the base it launched, as it did before the base could be decided beside. What remains of the refusal reads the start's own base mark, not a key on the decision. Cases stage the probe's sequence and show there is nothing to answer.

findings.issue: A base run whose processes die beside a writer decision leaves the decision stuck: the mark is folded but never marked done, the decision is never taken again, every re-render says the base is still running beside it, and the refusal says the spending answer opens once the base ends with a reading, which will never happen. `rerun` gets out, and nothing says so. Nothing is charged. Established by probe.
findings.resolution: Gone with the beside decision: a held red whose base run stopped without a reading is read as cut short on the next call, as a held base already was, and asks the base-unknown decision.

findings.issue: A gate that goes green while the base beside it is still running is never settled: the settle returns early because the mark is not done, the reviewer is dispatched, and when the base later ends as red-at-base no note is written, no verdict kept and the mark never decided. Ending before a slow background base is the likely order, and it is the case the note and the reviewer's section exist for. Established by probe; the changelog sentence about a gate gone green beside a base is false for it.
findings.resolution: Gone with the beside decision: no writer round runs while a base is unmeasured, so no gate can turn green over one; the settle path, its kept reading and the note's reader go if nothing reaches them, or stay with a case if something does.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py (ANSWER_SPENDS; the open-now list); the rule line of gate-red-base-unknown
findings.issue: The table of what an answer costs prices `resume` as free while it spends one of the start's bounded resume rounds and a paid session, and one rule line says a round spent in words the case holding the lines to the table does not recognise. The refusal and the printed decision list `resume` as open on the base-unknown decision when no session is recorded, and it is then refused for that reason.
findings.resolution: The table prices rounds as well as attempts and every rule line is held to it; the open-now list applies the session test.

findings.issue: The own-files skip trusts the runner's suite name: a file the task created that re-exports cases from a file the base has is read as the task's own red, with no base run. A suite name says where cases were collected, not where they come from. From reading; a question more than a defect.
findings.resolution: The skip's sentence says what it knows (the failing suite is a file the task created; where its cases come from is not read), so the person can ask for a base measurement; or the skip measures when the created file imports a test file the base has.

findings.issue: A base run whose recorded pid reads alive holds its red for ever, and the only advice printed names an answer the drive refuses. Probe: a base run killed and an unrelated live process's pid written into its launch record (what pid reuse looks like): every call prints wait-base with no age and no bound; `measure-base` and `block` answer that no decision is pending; running the printed run line again says the run already ran and to answer `measure-base`, the answer just refused; the hold ended only when the unrelated process exited. A pid whose state cannot be read (another user's process) reads alive the same way. The waiting code is as it was before this phase, but making a red wait for its base again makes it the only path for every red, and the misdirecting sentence is current.
findings.resolution: The wait has a way out the drive prints: a launch whose process started after it was launched, or that has waited past a bound read off the base's own recorded durations, is read as cut short and asks the base-unknown decision; and every sentence printed while waiting names only what is open at that moment. Cases for pid reuse and for an unreadable pid.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py (the refusal over a base that never leaves a reading)
findings.issue: A base run that dies on every measurement (killed, out of memory) is read as unknowable but measurable, so the answers that spend never open, and the bound that opens them counts only bases whose code moved: the person is left with measuring again (which dies again), rerun, block, or the owner's override, where before `resume` was still taken. And one shape was not staged end to end: a red whose record lacks the base's head while a kept base resolves, where measuring drops nothing and the next call asks the same refused decision.
findings.resolution: A base that stopped without a reading as many times as the bound allows counts toward it, and the decision then says the base was never measured and opens the spending answers; the unstaged shape is staged through its real producer and either reaches a way out or is fixed.

findings.file: tests/test_drive_phase.py (the hold's cases; the cost-line reading; the killed-base helper); PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md
findings.issue: Four holes in the cases. The hold in the gate step itself is untested: narrowing it survived every block because a second check catches the same state, and what only the first adds (a red's follower recipes do not run over an unmeasured base) has no case, since no fixture has a follower. The reading that holds each rule line's cost words to the cost table cannot read the table's own word for a round: a rule line saying a resume spends no session round passes. The helper that kills a base in one block still lacks the wait the other helper gained, so the known unstable case stays unstable. The build guide's case ranges stop one short in two places.
findings.resolution: A case with a follower on the red asserting nothing runs while the drive waits; the cost reading built from the table's own words, failing on a clause that names an answer with a cost it cannot classify; one kill helper; the ranges read off the suite.

findings.issue: The cost table is keyed by the answer's word alone, and one word has two costs: `resume` on the no-return ask resumes the agent and counts no round, while the table prices every `resume` as a session round, and the documents say so generally. Not reachable as a wrong refusal today; an inaccuracy in a table claimed to be the one statement of costs.
findings.resolution: The table is keyed by decision and answer, or that pair is an entry of its own, and the documents say which resume spends a round.

review.outcome: [findings: 67 - 4 high, 24 med, 39 low; 31 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: The browser jobs' time bound is about the slice: the Chromium install is timed by step and cached, and each bound's basis is re-measured
tasks.description:
The `browser (report)` job is bounded at 19 minutes on a recorded longest run of about nine, and on three runs in one day it took 17m44s once and was cut at the bound twice, the second time with the slice's VERIFY OK printed in the same second. Two costs sit in that job and in `browser (panel)` beside it. The install step (`npm ci`, then `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`) took between six and nine minutes. The slice took over eleven where its recorded longest whole job was nine.

Measure before changing: split the install into steps that each print their own duration (the package install, the browser download, the system packages) and read one run. Then remove what can be removed: cache the browser download keyed by the pinned playwright version in the lock file, and install only the system packages the runner image lacks. A cache miss must still install and pass; a cache hit must not skip a version change. tasks.title: A task's verdict is in its commit: Audit-Task, Audit-Gate, Audit-Run and Audit-Override trailers, written by the commit verb and read back from git alone
tasks.description:
The commit verb writes the verdict it bound the commit to into the commit itself. Today a task commit carries Audit-Row (a journal nonce) and an optional Co-Authored-By; which run graded it is known only through the evidence ledger and the journal. Add: Audit-Task: <task id>; Audit-Gate: <status> <gate digest>; Audit-Run: <runId>; and, when the verb was told to commit over a verdict, Audit-Override: <the reason, verbatim>. The values come from the one place that already decides them, the verdict binding the verb asks before it commits (_verdict_binding.binding): the trailers name the run the binding bound, never another, so a commit made in the phase tree after a wave member's bytes were integrated names the run that graded the phase tree's bytes. Audit-Row stays as it is.

Reading: _commit_trail.py gains the reader, over git log alone. A commit carrying Audit-Task and no Audit-Gate reads as no verdict recorded, never as passed. A commit carrying no Audit-Task (every commit made before this release, and every commit made by hand) is not a trailer commit and its verdict is read as before. Status (_status_facts.py) and the report (_evidence_view.py) read a done task's verdict at its commit from the trailers, and say which source they read.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A task commit made by the verb in a real git fixture carries the trailers, and `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns them.
2. In a clone of that fixture with the evidence directory removed, the reader returns the same task, status, digest and run.
3. Audit-Task without Audit-Gate reads as no verdict recorded; a status word this build does not know is reported as itself, never folded into passed or failed.
4. An override reason is carried verbatim. Decide what a reason holding a newline does by what git round-trips (a folded trailer, or a refusal naming the line) and pin it with a case; a silent truncation is the defect.
5. Status and the report render the same verdict from the trailers as from the row, on one fixture read both ways.
6. A commit made over a tree other than the one the bound run graded is refused as today; the new trailers do not weaken that refusal.
7. COMPATIBILITY.md states the four trailer names as read from this release on, and that Audit-Row and the co-author trailer are unchanged; CHANGELOG.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md describe what the commit now carries.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every reader of a task commit's message or trailers - _invariants.trailer_carriers and commits_carrying, the doctor's trail checks, drive-phase.py own_commit (it finds a task's commit through Audit-Row; it must keep working unchanged), close-phase.py, integrate-task.py, tools/check-git-pipeline.py (it drives the write half against a real repository and pins message shapes), and any suite asserting an exact commit message.

tasks.title: The newest run of a task or a phase is one record in its own shard, written by the gate under the phase lock
tasks.description:
Add the record that will replace the ledger row, beside the row, changing no reader yet. After a recorded run (run-test-gate.py --record, task or phase scope) the subject in its shard carries `lastRun`: the run's id, moments and durations (startedAt, durationMs, selectionMs), status and failed list, verdictSource and reusedFrom, the reuse key, the gate digest and source, leftToPhaseGate, the tested state (head, dirty, tree key), the banners and the machine and attribution lines, and per step: name, exit, ran, outcome, failing lines up to the existing cap, the measured duration when measured here, and reusedFrom when copied. A copied step carries its source's verdict fields forward, so the record is the newest measurement of each current step and no older record is needed to read it. `testEvidence` stays the three-key pointer and is written from the record in the same write. Replace, never append.

The write. Today the pointer write is skipped when the phase lock is held, because the ledger row stands anyway. A record that is the only copy cannot be skipped: the recorder takes the phase lock with a bounded wait behind any verb's write, and a record it still could not write is exit 3 naming the log path. Never exit 0 or 1 without the record. A verb that rewrites a task (move, reopen, group sign-off's copy of a carrier's pointer, reconcile) does to `lastRun` what it does to `testEvidence`.

The launch. `--launch <token>` is stored on the record, so a caller that started the run in the background can find the record of exactly that run.

Time. The recorder appends the gate and the selection stage to the task's `timing` itself, in the same locked write, from the same figures, citing the run by id; today the drive queues them in its own state from the ledger row. The stage survives the record's replacement.

ACCEPTANCE (each a case).
1. After five recorded runs of one gate a subject holds exactly one `lastRun`, its runId is the last one printed, and the shard is no larger than after the first run.
2. Exit 0 or 1 implies the shard's record names the printed runId and status; a lock that stays held past the wait is exit 3 naming the log, and the shard is unchanged.
3. `testEvidence` equals the pointer derived from `lastRun`; delete the pointer and reconcile restores it from the record.
4. A verb's write and a background record write, interleaved in both orders, both land: neither field is lost.
5. A recorded run changes no byte inside the content identity: the reuse key is the same before and after, and the set of paths the run modified (git status in a fixture) is exactly what recorded_paths names.
6. The record's size is bounded by the gate's width: failing lines per step at the existing cap, steps no more than declared plus derived. Print the measured bytes for this repository's own task gate in the outcome.
7. The schema accepts `lastRun` on a task and on a phase, a plan without it validates unchanged, and a one-file plan and a per-phase plan both carry it.
8. A machine path in a failing line reads scrubbed, as every string the shard write passes does, and the verdict fields are untouched.
9. The evidence row is still written, byte for byte as before, with the same runId as the record.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every reader of a task or phase object that copies, renders or validates its keys - validate-manifest.py and _manifest_rules.py, _manifest_io's split and join, audit-task.py's verbs named above, render-report.py and the panel's composition (an unknown key must not be rendered as content), tools/demo/gen-demo-manifest.py and the committed examples, tools/check-committed-pii.py (the record holds a head and failing lines), tools/check-example-ledgers.py, and drive-phase.py's timing queue (queue_row, row_stages, stage_args): once the recorder writes the stages, the drive must not write them a second time.

outcome.technical: THE WHOLE RECORD OF P169.3 (attempt 2; it replaces attempt 1's filing). WHAT THE TREE HOLDS. (a) The record. `_evidence_io`: RECORD_KEY `lastRun`. run_record builds the record from a row: runId, startedAt, durationMs, selectionMs, status, failed, verdictSource, reusedFrom, reuse key, gate digest, gateSource, leftToPhaseGate, banners, testedState {head, dirtyDigest, treeKey}, the machine and attribution lines, and launch. Each step keeps name, exit, ran, outcome, failing lines cut at MAX_FAILING, durationMs only when measured here, and reusedFrom when copied. A REUSED row copies its source's steps forward; steps are cut at MAX_STEPS with stepsDropped. tasks.title: Every reader of recorded runs goes through one reader over the shard records and the older rows, and answers the same from either
tasks.description:
`_evidence_io.read_rows` is the seam every reader of recorded runs already goes through (count its callers with grep before you start and put the count's command in the outcome). Make what it returns the union of the frozen ledger rows and the `lastRun` records of the plan's subjects, each record presented in the row's shape, one entry per runId (a run present as both is one entry). Then prove that nothing downstream needs the ledger: for a fixture holding records only and the same fixture holding rows only, each of these gives the same answer - the verdict binding (_verdict_binding.binding, with its reused row followed to the measured source), the step repeat (reusable_run, repeated_step_sources, step_parts) and its part-reused result, the reading of a red against the base (base_run), latest_by_subject, row_by_run, the gate's mean, the drive's read-back of a run it launched (green and red, with no commit made, and a red read back runs no step), close-phase's reading of a branch's runs (it reads the branch's ledger texts through git today; it must read the branch's shards the same way), and audit-task's --failing-from and couple --basis-run (resolve against records and rows, or refuse naming both places).

The drive finds the record of the run it launched by the launch token, not by comparing the subject's run ids against a list kept in its own state.

With one record per subject, a rule written over 'the newest row for the identity' has only one candidate; where a branch can no longer be reached (a newer row for the same identity), delete it and its case rather than leaving it unreachable, and name each deleted branch in the outcome.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. The table: every reader named above, records-only against rows-only, same answer.
2. A second ask on an unchanged tree, with records only, measures exactly the steps the left-out reading names and copies every other, each copy naming a run that measured it.
3. A record whose reuse key is not the current key repeats nothing.
4. The drive's decision read from the record equals the run's own --json for green and for red, with no commit made; reading a red back runs no gate step.
5. A reader of history that finds no older directory says so with a basis; it never prints a zero as if it had counted.
6. A plan and ledger as the previous release wrote them (use a committed example or build the fixture from real rows) give the same status, report and gate-condition answers before and after this change.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every caller of read_rows, row_by_run, latest_by_subject and oldest_first (the callers span the drive, the gate runner, audit-task.py, audit-lookup.py, full-gate.py, the doctor's trail and completion checks, the report, the panel, usage economics, propose-gates.py, validate-manifest.py's suite keys, record-outside-run.py, tools/plan-window.py, tools/gate-parity.py, tools/check-example-ledgers.py and the release guard under .claude/hooks). A caller that reads `rowFiles` or `files` to name where a run lives must still be able to: say what those mean for an entry that came from a shard.

tasks.title: The base is measured only when a red could predate the task, its verdict is kept per commit, and the writer is not held for it
tasks.description:
After a red task gate the drive measures the phase's base so that a red the base already has is not blamed on the task. Today that measurement is due whenever the reading is no-base or not-knowable, the red's decision is held until the base verdict exists, and the verdict lives in a base-scope ledger row, a progress record under the drive's state and a mark. State the rule as a property of the records and move the verdict where it survives.

Needed means all three: the task gate is red; some failing case or step is not one a file this task's `tests.add` created (a case the task itself added cannot predate it); and no clean-tree measurement of that step at that base commit is recorded. Otherwise no base run is started and the decision says which of the three made it unnecessary.

Kept means: the base verdict for a commit is in the plan (on the red task's record, keyed by the base commit, readable through the one reader), computed at most once per commit and step set, and a second red at the same base reads it.

Not held means: when a writer session exists to resume, the red's failing lines go to it at once, and the base runs beside it; if the base then shows the same red, the next decision says so and the writer is not resumed over it again. Where no session exists (the dispatched writer), the decision is offered with the base named as still running rather than withheld.

Keep what the phase before this one fixed: one liveness reading decides both the reading of a base run's record and the removal of its tree.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A red whose failing cases all live in files the task's tests.add created starts no base run, and the decision says why.
2. A second red at the same base commit and step set starts no base run and reads the kept verdict, which equals the first.
3. A red with a session to resume sends the failing lines before the base verdict exists; a base that then shows the same red produces the base decision and no further resume over that red.
4. A base run killed mid-way leaves no tree and no claim behind after the next call, as today.
5. The seconds: print, for one red on this repository's own plan, the wall time from the red to the writer's resume before and after, measured twice with a gap.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: run-test-gate.py base_red and base_reading, _evidence_io.base_run and its row keys (baseOf, baseRed), the drive's dispatch-base, wait-base, gate-red-base and gate-red-base-unknown decisions and every document that names them (the orchestrator reference and the phase command), audit-lookup.py's red lines, and the time record's base stage.
