The `steps` description gains 'Absent only when `sharedWithRepeated` names `steps`.', paid by cutting the `sharedWithRepeated` description's restatement of how steps are derived and its '(which `record_row` asks first)' clause. Help payload (tests/test__help.py _payload_bytes) 159688 at head -> 159665 now, limit PAYLOAD_CAP-PAYLOAD_HEADROOM = 160000. The $defs/lastRun top description is not in the payload (the $ref sibling's description is served), so trimming it pays nothing; that trim was reverted. _json_schema.py: `contains` added to SUPPORTED, `_check_contains`: at least one item admits (draft 2020-12 default minContains, so an empty list is refused), one reason per list, unread propagated, non-arrays left alone. MEASUREMENT (scratch scripts that read M.record_bytes; (b) = the stored record with `steps` put back from `_copied_steps(repeatedRun)` and dropped from sharedWithRepeated): live plan, 10 records: widest (a) 16807 = widest (b) 16807 (P169.20-6l3, which shares no steps), and the one shared-steps record P169.5 goes 9436 -> 15374 under (b). Worst-case fixture (whole repeat of a run at MAX_STEPS steps, each at MAX_FAILING+2 lines of 600 chars): (a) 34896, (b) 68416, past RECORD_MAX_BYTES 49152, because `steps` is in no position of RECORD_CUT_ORDER and bounded_record keeps a record still over its bound. Measured at 08:40:50/08:41:10 and again at 08:47:30, spread 0. (b) also cannot make the record already in docs/audit/phases/P169.json validate without editing it; (a) does, and sp1 is green. TODAY'S UNKNOWN KEYWORD: the reader does not silently skip it. check_findings returns it in `unread` (js3; `contains` itself came back as unread {'contains'} before this change). _manifest_rules._check_schema turns each unread keyword into a `rules.schema.unchecked` WARNING ('those values were NOT verified'), which validate-manifest --strict reads as a FINDING (is_schema_line). The gap: a caller of check_findings that ignores `unread` sees a pass. rk1 counts unread keywords as refusals for that reason. TESTS: tests/test__evidence_io.py rk-block (rk1-rk5, staged), composed through write_record/keep_base/run_record/finished_record in fresh git fixtures; tests/test__json_schema.py contains row in KEYWORD_ROWS + js12. SHAPES and their tables: measured (lines+launch), part repeat, whole repeat sharing every equal subtree, whole repeat keeping its own reach, whole repeat of the record it replaces (carried under the lock), repeat whose source neither holds (repeatedRunUnread), steps cut at MAX_STEPS (stepsDropped), record replacing launched runs (replacedLaunches), red with kept base runs (keep_base), red with a settled base reading, phase-scope record, phase-scope whole repeat, and one record per bound that cuts one more RECORD_CUT_ORDER field (composed as keep_base composes: finished_record over a part repeat with every observation and a kept base run). rk2 derives its tables: RECORD_CUT_ORDER (each entry must be the one field some bound newly cut), shareable = keys of a measured record outside _NEVER_SHARED holding a dict/list longer than its path (_shared_paths' rule) + steps, record-shaped = _RECORD_SHAPED + RECORD_LINE_KEYS + REPEAT_UNREAD_KEY, REPLACED_KEY, LAUNCH_KEY, BASE_RUNS_KEY. rk3: every stored pointer equals pointer_from_record and pointer_for of every row, each validated against $defs/testEvidence. rk4: the twin. rk5: tasks' and phases' lastRun are each a $ref to $defs/lastRun, so ONE definition across the three places. MUTATIONS (scratch copy outside the checkout, each anchor counted once, landed confirmed, __pycache__ purged, restored in the same run): writer stores steps without naming them in sharedWithRepeated -> rk1, rk2, rk4 red; writer drops `at` -> rk1-rk4 red; schema arm 1 loses required [steps] (steps excused unconditionally) -> rk4 alone red, rk1 green; `contains` always admits -> js1 red; never admits -> rk1 red; unmutated copy all green. READERS OF THE STORED FORM: subject_records (raw; used by reconcile for at/runId/pointer only), _reconciled (runId/at, pointer_from_record), pointer_from_record (runId/status/at, all in _NEVER_SHARED), _put_record (runId, launch/replacedLaunches via replaced_launches, record_row for the carry), keep_base/carry_kept_bases (resolved_shared), records_of_bodies (record_row, which resolves first; repeatedRun read whole, never shared into), run_by_launch (rows), audit-task.py _group_record/signoff (copies the stored record whole + gradedBy, sharing intact, reads no steps), gen-demo-manifest _recorded (writes run_record; demo has no repeats). The panel, report, status and doctor never read lastRun: grep of plugins/audit/scripts (ui JS included), hooks, tools and .claude/hooks for RECORD_KEY|lastRun shows no other reader. They read through read_rows/record_row. No reader shows 'no steps' for a shared record, so nothing needed fixing. 4.0.0 TIER: the word is BUG_VALUE_REFUSAL_RELEASE = '4.0.0' (_manifest_crossrefs.py:656, re-exported _manifest_rules.py:221), used only in the warning sentence. tasks.title: While the base of a red is unmeasured the drive accepts no answer that spends and charges the task nothing: one check where answers are applied, read from the table of what each answer costs, with the set-aside repair of the base decisions carried forward
tasks.description:
This task carries forward a repair that was written, reviewed and set aside, and finishes it. Read three things before designing, in this order.

1. THE CLASS. The commit that stopped holding a red for a base run measured in the background (`git log --oneline -8`, the one titled "The base is measured only when a red could predate the task") was reviewed twice. Both reviews found the same class: something the drive does while the base of a red is skipped, unread or still running changes who the red is charged to, or costs the task what a held base would not have. The phase's findings P169-R41 to R49 (first review) and R51 to R55 (second review, of the repair) carry every scenario with the probe that established it.

2. THE SAVED REPAIR. The patch file the orchestrator names in its prompt (the cancelled task P169.20-6l3 records where it is kept) is the whole earlier repair (twelve files; it applies cleanly to the branch head: `git apply --check` it, then apply it with `git apply`, which is the one write to the checkout you make without the Edit tool; every later edit goes through Edit). It was green on its own gate, proved ten mutations, and settles R42's first three shapes, R43, R44, R45, R46, R47, R48 and R49. Its decision table `BASE_TURNS` and `base_turn` are a starting point, not a constraint: the second review found that only two of its six call sites compute a pair, that the others use the table as a switch beside conditions that still decide, and that its default is dead code.

3. WHY IT WAS NOT ENOUGH (P169-R51, high). The repair limited the decision taken beside a running base to the writer decision "because its resume spends nothing", but that decision also offers `retry`, which spends an attempt over an unmeasured base. The rule was put on the NAME of the decision; the thing that spends is the ANSWER. This is the second time the same class was fixed in one place and found open in the next, so by this repository's rule the fix is now an invariant, not another row.

THE INVARIANT, to be stated once above the code and enforced in ONE place:
   While the base of a start's red is unmeasured (skipped as not needed is "measured" only by the rules of the saved repair; running, never started, killed, replaced, or kept-but-unread are all unmeasured), the drive accepts no answer that spends, whatever decision offered it, and charges nothing to the task.
 "Spends" is read from the drive's own table of what each answer costs (find it: the sentences "retry spends one", "rerun spends no attempt" come from somewhere; if the cost of an answer lives only in prose today, making it a table that both the prose and the check read is part of this task). The check sits where an answer is applied, before anything is written, and its refusal spends nothing, exits the way the drive's existing "answers nothing" refusals exit, and says which answers are open now and that the others open when the base ends. Decide and state whether the decision printed beside a base should also OMIT the answers it would refuse (it should not offer what it will refuse; but the refusal stays, since a decision can be answered late).
 The case that holds it is derived, not enumerated: for every decision the drive can print for a red (from `DECISIONS`), for every answer that decision offers, with the base in each unmeasured state, assert the attempt count and the resume-round count before and after, and that no writer or executor was dispatched by a spending answer. A decision or answer added to the tables later is covered without anyone adding a case; one the case cannot stage fails it by name.

ALSO OWED (second review).
 - R52: the own-files skip must hold only for a path the base commit's tree lacks AND that the task did not arrive at by renaming or copying a base file (ask git with rename detection); compare the way the filesystem compares (a case-insensitive filesystem holds `Tests/X.py` and `tests/x.py` as one file); a symlink measures. Each with the twin that still skips.
 - R53: a settled reading is kept and noted only against the red it was measured for; a mark that joined another start's base run is decided and keeps nothing it did not measure.
 - R54: each sentence says what the code knows (the green-over-base-red note does not name a cause it did not observe; a replaced launch is not "ended"; the joined-unread sentence; the join's line for a run that never started; the documents say WHICH starts join).
 - R55: cases for a green gate whose base mark is already decided or still running; the table total by construction rather than by a dead default; a case in the gate runner's own suite for a base step that reached no verdict.
 - The table: either every site that reads a base mark's state decides through it, or say plainly in its comment which sites decide by their own condition and why that is safe. A table that is a comment beside the code is the thing the second review caught.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. Every finding R41 to R49 and R51 to R55 has a case red at the branch head (before the patch) or, for those the patch already settles, red at the head and green with the patch; R51 to R55 red WITH the patch applied and green after your change. Say which is which.
2. Mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed: the invariant's check removed; `retry` beside a base applied; the spend table saying `retry` costs nothing; a renamed file read as the task's own; a joined mark keeping a reading; plus the saved repair's ten, re-run against the final code.
3. plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md sits exactly at its context ceiling: `python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate` stays green, a byte added there is a byte cut there. The help payload's budget (`tests/test__help.py` p5) has almost no room: a schema description you add is paid for by one you shorten.
4. The drive suite is staged and long, and one of its cases (bq4, a base run killed while it measures) is known to fail once in a while under load: if it is the only red of a run, run its block again alone twice and report all three results rather than calling it green or red.
5. Full sweep green with no exception, after the last edit.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every decision and step the drive prints for a red and for a base (`gate-red`, `gate-red-writer`, `gate-red-base`, `gate-red-base-unknown`, `dispatch-base`, `wait-base`) and the documents that name them or their answers; the `auto` mode's choice among answers (it must never choose one the invariant refuses: check it and say); `run-test-gate.py --base-of` and `--kept-only`; the time record's base stage (once per measurement); the cancelled-gate bound and the replaced-launch path where they meet a base mark; the reviewer's brief and the sign-off (the note's reader, in audit-lookup.py); the schema's `lastRun.baseRed` description and the suites that hold its vocabulary.

If a file you need is outside your list, STOP BEFORE FILING and hand back the exact change with the reason: a return is filed once per start.

tasks.title: A red waits for its base: the drive no longer decides a red beside a base run still measuring, so nothing is charged or decided while a base is unmeasured, by construction
tasks.description:
Three independent reviews in a row found the same class in the same feature, each time in the place the previous repair did not look: first a plain red decision answered with `retry` beside a running base (P169-R41), then `retry` on the writer decision beside it (P169-R51), then a decision produced elsewhere (the no-return ask after a resumed round) that goes past the refusal because only the red-gate decision records the key the refusal reads (P169-R59), with two more consequences of the same state (a killed base leaves the decision stuck, R60; a gate gone green before the base ends is never settled, R61). Each repair was sound for what it covered. The feature's state space (decisions x answers x who produced the decision x what the base is doing x green or red x waves) is what keeps producing the next one.

THE DECISION THIS TASK CARRIES OUT: the drive no longer decides a red beside a base run that is still measuring. A red whose base is being measured WAITS for it (`wait-base`), as it did before this phase. Then the invariant "nothing is charged to a task, and nothing about its red is decided, while the base of that red is unmeasured" holds by construction: there is no pending decision to answer, no writer round to run, no gate to turn green, while a base runs. The measured basis for giving the feature up is in the phase's records: on this repository's recorded runs the beside decision applied to no red at all (every recorded red took the agent path), and its derived saving on the session-writer path was the base run's own duration, which the same phase already cut by measuring only the red steps. The feature is not lost: it is recorded for the session-per-task design, where a task has its own tree and the writer is a session, with what these three reviews established as its entry conditions.

WHAT STAYS (all of it is on the branch head, and none of it depends on deciding beside a base): a base run is not started for a red in files the task created and the base lacks (with the rename, letter-case and symlink readings); a red whose steps a recorded or kept base run already measured reads that run; a measured base is kept on the red's record; a base step that reached no verdict is not "measured"; a start joins a base run already measuring its commit rather than launching a second; `keep_base` refuses another commit.

WHAT GOES: every path by which a decision about a red is taken, printed, answered, re-taken or settled while its base runs: the beside turn in the decision table, the rule telling the orchestrator to call next at once after `dispatch-base`, the beside mark and its end detection, the re-take of a beside decision, the count of rounds resumed beside a base and its sentence, the refusal of a late answer to a beside decision, and the green-over-running-base settle. For each of the following, decide by REACHABILITY and say which way it went and why: the settle on a green gate with its kept reading (`settledOf`), the dated note and its reader in the reviewer's brief and the sign-off (with every red held until its base is read, can a gate still go green over a base mark that is ended and undecided? if nothing reaches it, it goes, with its record key, its schema sentence and its composed record shape; if something does, it stays with a case that reaches it by that path); the refusal of a spending answer over an unmeasured base (it still has one real subject: the base-unknown decision, where the base can still be measured and `retry` is offered; keep the refusal for that, reading the START'S OWN BASE MARK in the drive's state rather than a key on the decision, so that any decision for that task, whoever produced it, is covered; a decision with no record of what its base stands on fails closed).
 Dead code is removed, not left behind a switch: no option, no flag, no table row that nothing takes.

ALSO OWED.
 - R62: the table of what an answer costs prices resume rounds as well as attempts; every rule line and every sentence that names a cost is held to it by the case that already holds the attempt wording (extend its reading rather than adding a second one); the list of answers open now applies the same session test the refusal applies.
 - R63: the own-files skip's sentence says what it knows: the failing suite is a file the task created and the base lacks; where the cases in it come from is not read. State whether measuring when the created file imports a test file the base has is worth its cost, with a count from this repository's recorded reds (read only, the command in the outcome, the number in no document); do it only if that count says so.
 - The three probes of the third review become cases: the resumed round with no result, the killed base, the gate green before the base ends. With the beside decision gone each must show there was nothing to answer or settle at that point, and each must be red at the branch head.

ACCEPTANCE.
1. A derived case: for every decision the drive can print for a task (all of `DECISIONS`, not only the red ones), staged while that task's start holds a base mark that is launched and not ended, no answer is accepted that spends (from the cost table) and none dispatches a writer or an executor; in practice the drive prints `wait-base` and no decision at all, and the case asserts that first. A decision it cannot stage in that state fails by name.
2. Mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed: the hold removed for the writer decision; the hold removed for the plain red; the refusal reading a key on the decision instead of the base mark; the cost table pricing resume as free; plus the earlier repairs' mutations that still have a subject, re-run against the final code (say which no longer have one, and why).
3. plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md sits exactly at its context ceiling and its paragraph on the base decision changes (it says "only resume beside it"): the reworded paragraph is no longer than the one it replaces, and `python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate` stays green. The executor reference, the build guide and the changelog describe one behaviour: a red waits for its base. The changelog's Unreleased entries about the beside decision are rewritten to what ships, not appended to: a reader of the release notes must not meet a feature and its removal.
4. Bytes: a record key that goes makes the widest record no wider; measured twice with a gap, in the outcome.
5. Wall time, said honestly in the outcome: what a red now waits on this repository's recorded base durations (the commands from the earlier accounts are in the phase's returns), and that this is the same wait as before the phase minus the base runs the skip rules avoid.
6. Full sweep green with no exception, after the last edit.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: every decision and step the drive prints for a red and for a base and the documents that name them or their answers; `run-test-gate.py --base-of` and `--kept-only`; the time record's base stage (queued once per measurement: with no beside path, by which call); the join of an earlier start's base; the cancelled-gate bound and the replaced-launch path where they meet a base mark; the reviewer's brief and the sign-off if the note's reader goes; the schema's `lastRun.baseRed` description, the composed record shapes that hold every record to the schema (a key that goes leaves the tables and its shape), and the vocabulary suites.

tasks.title: A wait for a base run has an exit the drive prints: a launch whose process cannot have been its own, or that has waited past a bound read off recorded runs, is cut short, and no sentence printed while waiting names an answer that is refused
tasks.description:
A red now waits for its base run again, and an independent review could not get anything decided or charged while it waits. What it found is the other side of that: the wait itself has no way out when the base run's process can never be read as ended, and the sentences printed meanwhile point at an answer the drive refuses. The phase's findings P169-R64 (medium) and R65 to R67 (lows) carry each with its probe; the reviewer's probes are named in the orchestrator's prompt.

THE RULE: every state the drive can wait in for a base run has an exit the drive itself prints, and every sentence printed while it waits names only what is open at that moment.

1. R64, the wait. A launch whose recorded pid reads alive holds for ever: after a pid is reused by an unrelated process, or when the pid's state cannot be read (another user's process), `wait-base` repeats with no age and no bound; `measure-base` and `block` answer that no decision is pending; the printed run line, run again, says the run already ran and to answer `measure-base`, which was just refused. Required: (a) a launch is read as cut short, and the base-unknown decision asked, when the process holding its pid started AFTER the launch was recorded (read the process's start time where the platform gives it; say what each platform gives and what happens where it gives nothing), or when the wait has passed a bound derived from the base's own recorded durations (find how the drive already decides foreground against background from a recorded mean and how gates time out, and derive from that rather than inventing a number; say the bound's basis in the sentence that announces it); (b) `wait-base` says how long it has waited and when the bound falls; (c) the already-ran refusal names something open. Do not change what a healthy wait prints beyond the age, and prove a base run that is slow but alive is NOT cut short inside its bound.
2. R65, a base that never leaves a reading. A base run that dies on every measurement stays "unknowable but measurable", so the answers that spend never open and the bound that opens them counts only bases whose code moved. Required: a base run that stopped without a reading counts toward that bound, and past it the decision says the base was never measured, by how many tries, and opens the spending answers. Also stage, through its real producer and not through stubs, the shape the review could not: a red whose record lacks the base's head while a kept base resolves (the review reads it as asking the same refused decision again after `measure-base`); it either reaches an exit or is fixed.
3. R66, the cases. A case with a follower recipe on the red asserting nothing of it runs while the drive waits (today narrowing the gate step's own hold survives every block); the reading that holds each rule line's cost words to the cost table is built from the table's own words and fails on a clause naming an answer with a cost it cannot classify (today "resume spends no session round" passes); the base-killing helper used by case bq4 goes through the one helper that waits for the drive's liveness reading (that case has cost a gate run in three phases); the build guide's case ranges are read off the suite.
4. R67, the cost table is keyed by decision and answer where one word has two costs (`resume` on the no-return ask resumes the agent and counts no round), and the documents say which resume spends a round.

ACCEPTANCE. Each point has a case red at the branch head and green after; the pid-reuse and unreadable-pid probes become cases through the drive's real liveness reading (a stub only for the clock and the process table, with the stubbed shapes taken from what the real reading returns on this platform); mutations on scratch copies outside every checkout, restored in the same command, each confirmed landed: the age bound removed; the start-time check inverted; a slow live base cut short; a stopped base not counted toward the bound; the hold in the gate step narrowed (must now go red by the follower case); a cost clause the reading cannot classify accepted. plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md has three bytes under its context ceiling: `python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate` stays green, and a signal or step you reword there does not grow. Full sweep green with no exception after the last edit.

DEPENDANTS to answer for by name: `wait-base`, `dispatch-base`, `gate-red-base-unknown` and `measure-base` and every document naming them; the sweep of base trees and the release of a base launch's claim when a wait is cut short (no tree and no claim left behind: the killed-base cases already assert this for a killed run); the join of an earlier start's base (a joined wait is cut short by the same rule); the time record's base stage for a wait that was cut short; the cancelled-gate bound, which counts a different thing and must not be merged with this one; Windows, where the pid probe is another path (say what the case covers there and hand the orchestrator the command and expected output for a run on a Windows machine if a path cannot be exercised here).
